rationale: A macOS tracking area is not occluded by subviews, so a host that attaches a native child view still receives mouseMoved for every pointer position over that child. The host hit-tested its own root and published the arrow cursor unconditionally, wiping the child's cursor on every button-less move -- which is why a pointer only appeared to pick up the right icon after a mouse down, since the drag path publishes the captured cursor and no mouseMoved arrives mid-drag. The fix declines to publish when the point lies inside an attached native child, leaving the cursor owned by whoever actually draws there; the drag and no-child paths are unchanged. render-assets-and-backends is crossed by core/view only -- the three mac host translation units plus an added mac platform test that asserts the cursor changes on a stationary hover rather than only on mousedown. No renderer, backend, font, asset or Skia pin changes; no fixture, snapshot or threshold moves. Registered as watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a change that crossed its selector. No authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes.
